parts.title: Part I – Multiple Choice Questions
parts.instructions: Part I contains 80 multiple-choice questions (1 point each). Choose the one best answer and blacken its letter on the answer sheet. Questions 71–80 refer to the contour map in the figure (scale 1 cm to 4 km; contour values in metres). NOTE: items 46–50 (printed page 10) are missing from the only available scan and are stored as ‘not available’ placeholders.

parts.title: Part II – Short Answer Questions
parts.instructions: Part II contains ten short-answer questions (20 points in total; item 5 carries 1 point and item 8 carries 3 points). Answer all of them in the spaces provided.

exam.answer_key_note: No official key exists. All answers were solved independently and checked against the Eritrean MoE Geography textbooks Grades 9–12 (extracted text with page markers). Items with two defensible options accept both and carry a review_flag.

questions.stem: The first Greek scholar who measured the circumference of the earth was
explanation_steps: The textbook: Eratosthenes, a Greek scholar, measured the circumference of the earth; Herodotus described the physical and human geography of his day; Aristotle discussed earth processes.
Answer: B.
tips: Eratosthenes = circumference; Herodotus = father of geography (description).

similar_questions.stem: The Greek scholar called the 'father of geography' who described the physical and human geography of his day was
explanation_steps: Textbook: Herodotus. Answer: B.

questions.stem: An atmospheric gas that contributes most to the global warming is
explanation_steps: Carbon dioxide, released mainly by burning fossil fuels and deforestation, is the greenhouse gas responsible for most of the human-caused warming.
Nitrogen and oxygen (99% of the air) are not greenhouse gases; ozone is a minor greenhouse gas. Answer: C.
tips: Greenhouse gases: CO₂, methane, nitrous oxide, CFCs, water vapour.

similar_questions.stem: Which human activity adds most carbon dioxide to the atmosphere?
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

questions.stem: People who belong to the Saho ethnic group are dominantly found in the
explanation_steps: Textbook Table 7.4 (size and distribution of ethnic groups): Saho – about 5% – Debub and Northern Red Sea.
Of the options only Debub is listed. Answer: C.
tips: Distribution: Tigrinya – Maekel, Debub; Tigre – NRS, Anseba, Gash-Barka; Saho – Debub, NRS; Afar – SRS/NRS; Bilen – Anseba; Kunama, Nara – Gash-Barka.

similar_questions.stem: The Kunama and Nara ethnic groups live mainly in
explanation_steps: Textbook Table 7.4. Answer: B.

questions.stem: One of the following is an example of a natural feature.
explanation_steps: Natural (physical) features are made by nature: rivers, mountains, lakes, forests.
Schools, hospitals, towns and markets are human (cultural) features. Answer: D.
tips: Physical geography = natural features; human geography = man-made features.

similar_questions.stem: Which of these is a human (cultural) feature?
explanation_steps: Railways are built by people. Answer: C.

questions.stem: The type of renewable energy that has the <u>highest</u> potential in Eritrea is
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Eritrea has huge potential for solar energy due to its tropical location.' Several solar panels are already installed for villages, schools and clinics.
Wind (Assab coast) and geothermal (Alid, Danakil) potentials are local; rivers are seasonal, so hydro potential is small. Answer: B.
tips: Tropical latitude + many sunny days = solar.

similar_questions.stem: Why does Eritrea have little potential for hydro-electric power?
explanation_steps: Most rivers flow only in the rainy season. Answer: A.

questions.stem: ________ is a sub-division of physical geography that studies the distribution of plants and animals.
explanation_steps: The textbook (fields of physical geography): biogeography studies the distribution of plants and animals.
Answer: C.
tips: bio = life.

similar_questions.stem: The sub-division of physical geography that studies soils is
explanation_steps: Answer: A.

questions.stem: Which of the following rivers of Eritrea, flows eastward?
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'River Labka originates south-west of Geleb. It flows east and passes Marsa Kube before it enters the Red Sea.'
Gash, Mereb, Barka and Anseba drain west/north-west towards Sudan. Answer: B.
tips: Red Sea drainage: Labka, Falket, Wekiro, Haddas, Comayle.

similar_questions.stem: Which Eritrean river drains into the Red Sea?
explanation_steps: Textbook: Haddas cuts the escarpment and reaches the Red Sea. Answer: C.

questions.stem: Which of the following resources may be considered a renewable resource?
explanation_steps: The textbook: renewable (flow) resources include crops, trees, animals, soil, wind and solar energy; oil, gold and copper are non-renewable (fund) resources.
Timber comes from trees, which can be replanted. Answer: D.
tips: Renewable = can be restored with good management.

similar_questions.stem: Which is a non-renewable resource?
explanation_steps: Answer: C.

questions.stem: A settlement that consists of about a dozen of houses is a
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Hamlets consist of a dozen of houses or less… Villages are larger rural settlements consisting of dozens of houses and public buildings.'
Answer: C.
tips: Size order: isolated building < hamlet < village < town < city.

similar_questions.stem: Rural settlements are classified by size into isolated buildings, hamlets and
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

questions.stem: The surface temperature of our sun is estimated to be
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'The surface temperature of the sun reaches up to 6000 °C, which is the major source of light and heat energy.'
Answer: C.
tips: Sun: diameter ≈ 1,392,000 km (≈ 110 × Earth), surface ≈ 6000 °C.

similar_questions.stem: The sun's diameter is roughly how many times the earth's?
explanation_steps: Textbook: about 110 times. Answer: C.

questions.stem: Tsunami is a destructive water wave in the coastal areas caused by
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'An earthquake on the ocean floor can cause tremendous destructive waves called tsunamis' (e.g. the Indian Ocean tsunami of 26 December 2004).
Answer: D.
tips: Tsunami = sea-floor earthquake (also undersea volcanoes or landslides).

similar_questions.stem: The 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami was triggered by
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

questions.stem: The submerged part of a continent is called
explanation_steps: The continental shelf is the gently sloping, shallow (to about 200 m) edge of a continent covered by the sea.
The continental slope is the steep drop beyond it to the ocean floor. Answer: A.
tips: Shelf (shallow, rich fishing) → slope → deep ocean floor.

similar_questions.stem: The steep descent from the edge of the continental shelf to the deep ocean floor is the
explanation_steps: Answer: A.

questions.stem: Magma erupts into the surface of the earth through ________ of the crust.
explanation_steps: Magma reaches the surface through any opening in the crust: a central vent (pipe) of a volcano or long fissures/cracks/fractures (fissure eruptions).
All four words name such openings. Answer: E.
tips: Central eruption – through a vent; fissure eruption – through long cracks (forms lava plateaus).

similar_questions.stem: Lava plateaus are mostly formed by
explanation_steps: Lava pours out quietly from long fissures. Answer: B.

questions.review_flag: Keyed E (all are openings); a student following the textbook's 'vent' term might choose C.

questions.stem: The space between soil particles is called
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Porosity is the amount of space between soil particles. It measures the capacity of soil to hold water and air. Permeability is the ease with which water can move through soil.'
Answer: A.
tips: Porosity = space; permeability = flow; texture = particle size.

similar_questions.stem: The ease with which water moves through soil is called
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

questions.stem: Deposition along the Red Sea coast of Eritrea is the result of materials transported by
explanation_steps: The coastal plain is built mainly of alluvium brought down the eastern escarpment by seasonal streams (e.g. Wadi Laba, Haddas, Comayle), which spread it as alluvial fans and deltas.
Waves also deposit sand along beaches, so D is defensible; glaciers are absent. Keyed B; D also accepted.
tips: Coastal plain soils = alluvial deposits of escarpment streams; beaches/spits = wave deposits.

similar_questions.stem: A fan-shaped deposit formed where a stream leaves the escarpment onto a plain is an
explanation_steps: Answer: A.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 7 – Relief and Drainage Systems in Eritrea
textbook_ref.note: Textbook describes the coastal plains and flood-fed farming but does not name the agent of deposition.

questions.review_flag: Both streams (alluvium from the escarpment) and waves (beach deposits) deposit on the coast. Keyed B, D also accepted – teacher decision.

questions.stem: The only known planet in the solar system that supports human life is
explanation_steps: Only the Earth has liquid water, an oxygen-rich atmosphere and suitable temperatures for life.
Answer: C.
tips: Planets from the sun: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.

similar_questions.stem: The largest planet in the solar system is
explanation_steps: Answer: C.

questions.stem: A mound of wind-deposited sand is called
explanation_steps: The textbook (wind deposition): sand dunes are mounds or ridges of sand deposited by wind; loess is a deposit of fine wind-blown dust.
Mushroom rocks, zeugen and inselbergs are erosional features. Answer: E.
tips: Wind erosion features: mushroom rock, zeugen, yardang, inselberg. Wind deposits: dunes (barchan, seif), loess.

similar_questions.stem: A crescent-shaped sand dune is called a
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

questions.stem: ________ is a form of precipitation where snow comes mixed with the rain.
explanation_steps: Sleet is a mixture of rain and snow (or partly melted snow/ice pellets).
Hail is layered balls of ice from cumulonimbus clouds. Answer: D.
tips: Precipitation forms: rain, snow, sleet, hail (also dew, frost).

similar_questions.stem: Balls of ice formed in cumulonimbus clouds by repeated up-and-down movement are
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

questions.stem: The soil particle that remains suspended as a river enters the ocean is
explanation_steps: When a river enters the sea it slows and drops its load in order of size: boulders and pebbles first, then sand, then silt; the finest particles, clay (< 0.002 mm), stay in suspension longest and are carried out to sea.
The textbook groups silt and clay together as suspended load, so C is also accepted. Keyed D; C also accepted.
tips: Deposition order: coarse first, fine last.

similar_questions.stem: Which load is deposited first when a river slows down?
explanation_steps: The heaviest particles drop first. Answer: D.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 2 – Gradation by Rivers and Winds

questions.review_flag: Silt (C) and clay (D) are both suspended load; keyed D (finest, stays suspended longest), C also accepted. Option E prints 'peddle' (pebble).

questions.stem: The most widely used economic measure of development is
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Per capita income is a widely used economic measure of development. It is the total yearly income of a country… divided by its total population.' (The textbook's review question keys 'per capita income' as the most widely used measure.)
Answer: A.
tips: Total GNP/GDP ignores population size; per capita income divides by population.

similar_questions.stem: Per capita income is calculated as
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

questions.stem: One of the following <u>is not</u> a determinant factor for the establishment of a town.
explanation_steps: Towns grow at ports, mining centres, railway junctions, navigable rivers, crossroads and administrative centres – places with trade or employment.
A forested area does not in itself attract urban growth. Answer: B.
tips: Town functions: port, mining, route centre, market, administrative, resort.

similar_questions.stem: A town that grew because of nearby mineral deposits is a
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which of the following map scales is the largest?
explanation_steps: The larger the scale, the smaller the denominator of the representative fraction (1/100,000 is the biggest fraction).
Answer: A.
tips: Large scale = small area, more detail = small denominator.

similar_questions.stem: Which scale shows the MOST detail?
explanation_steps: Smallest denominator = largest scale. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Wind speed is usually expressed in
explanation_steps: Meteorological services measure wind with an anemometer and report speed in metres per second (SI unit) or knots; weather reports for the public often use kilometres per hour.
Both A and D are common units, so both are accepted. Keyed A; D also accepted.

similar_questions.stem: A wind of 10 m/s equals
explanation_steps: 10 × 3.6 = 36 km/h. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.note: Textbook discusses factors of wind speed but not its unit.

questions.review_flag: Both m/s (A) and km/h (D) are standard units; keyed A, D also accepted – teacher decision.

questions.stem: A method of soil conservation where steep slopes are leveled into a series of wide steps is
explanation_steps: Terracing cuts a steep slope into a series of flat steps (terraces) that slow run-off and hold soil – widely used in the Eritrean highlands.
Answer: D.
tips: Terraces = steps; contour ploughing = furrows across the slope.

similar_questions.stem: Rows of trees planted to reduce wind erosion are called
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

questions.stem: The geological process that creates deep-sea trenches is called
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'When two ocean floors collide, one sinks below the other and forms a deep trench in the ocean floor.' The sinking of one plate under another is subduction.
Answer: D.
tips: Convergent plates → subduction → trench + volcanoes + earthquakes.

similar_questions.stem: The Mariana Trench was formed at a
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

questions.stem: The transfer of heat from one object to another through contact is called
explanation_steps: Conduction = heat passed by direct contact (e.g. the ground warming the air touching it). Convection = transfer by moving currents of air/liquid; radiation = transfer by waves without contact.
Answer: C.
tips: Contact → conduction; currents → convection; waves → radiation.

similar_questions.stem: The sun heats the earth mainly by
explanation_steps: Answer: C.

questions.stem: Desertification, the spread of arid-like conditions, is mainly caused by
explanation_steps: Removing trees (for fuel, farmland, building) exposes the soil to erosion, reduces moisture and leads to desert-like conditions; overgrazing and over-cultivation add to it.
Afforestation, reforestation and crop rotation are remedies. Answer: C.
tips: Causes: deforestation, overgrazing, over-cultivation, drought.

similar_questions.stem: Which measure helps to fight desertification?
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

questions.stem: The administrative region in Eritrea with the highest number of sub-zones is
explanation_steps: Textbook Table 6.1: Maekel 7, Debub 14, Anseba 10, Southern Red Sea 4, Northern Red Sea 10, Gash-Barka 14 (total 59).
Gash-Barka ties with Debub but is not an option, so Debub. Answer: C.
tips: 6 zobas, 59 sub-zones (textbook).

similar_questions.stem: Which zoba has the fewest sub-zones according to the textbook?
explanation_steps: Southern Red Sea has 4. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 6 – Strategic Position, Size and Shape of Eritrea

questions.review_flag: Debub and Gash-Barka both have 14 sub-zones in the textbook; only Debub is offered.

questions.stem: Consider the following temperature data for a certain place. Daily Maximum Temperature = 24.6°C; Daily Minimum Temperature = 6.8°C. What is the daily range of temperature of the place?
explanation_steps: Daily range = maximum − minimum = 24.6 − 6.8 = 17.8 °C.
(31.4 is the sum; the mean would be 15.7 °C.) Answer: D.
tips: Range = max − min; mean = (max + min) ÷ 2.

questions.stem: A large proportion of the earth’s freshwater is found in the
explanation_steps: About 97% of all water is salt water in the oceans. Of the fresh water, about two-thirds is frozen in glaciers and ice caps (Antarctica, Greenland).
Answer: D.
tips: Oceans are salt; most fresh water is ice.

similar_questions.stem: Most of the earth's water (about 97%) is found in
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

questions.stem: The highlands of Eritrea occupy the central portion of the country stretching from
explanation_steps: The textbook: the Highlands 'occupy the central portion of the country extending from south to north. They separate the Western Lowlands and the Eastern Lowlands and form a major watershed.'
Answer: A.
tips: Highlands = central N–S backbone and watershed.

similar_questions.stem: The Eritrean highlands separate the
explanation_steps: Answer: A.

questions.stem: The layer of atmosphere that affects human activities <u>most</u> is the
explanation_steps: The troposphere is the lowest layer (up to about 8–18 km). It holds almost all water vapour, clouds and weather, and we live in it.
Answer: A.
tips: Weather happens in the troposphere; the ozone layer is in the stratosphere.

similar_questions.stem: In the troposphere, temperature
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which of the following physiographic divisions of Eritrea receives the <u>highest</u> rainfall?
explanation_steps: The textbook: rainfall 'exceptionally exceeds 1000 mm in the Green Belt Zone (Semenawi Bahri)' of the eastern Escarpment, which gets winter rain from the north-east trade winds (and its upper part summer rain too).
The highlands average 500–700 mm; the western lowlands 200–700 mm. Answer: C.
tips: Green Belt (Filfil, Solomuna) = wettest part of Eritrea – two rainy seasons.

similar_questions.stem: The eastern escarpment gets its winter rainfall from the

options.B: north-east trade winds crossing the Red Sea

explanation_steps: Answer: B.

questions.stem: The <u>most</u> densely populated continent in the world is
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Asia with a density of 129 persons per square kilometer was the most densely populated continent of the world. Europe and Africa had only 32 and 33 persons per square kilometer.'
Asia is not among the options, so 'None of the above'. Answer: E.
tips: Check whether the obvious answer (Asia) is actually offered.

similar_questions.stem: The most populous continent is
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

questions.review_flag: Europe (B) is a tempting distractor, but by the textbook's figures Africa (33/km²) is even slightly denser than Europe (32/km²); the correct continent, Asia, is not offered, so E.

questions.stem: Which of the following Precambrian rocks is believed to be the <u>oldest</u>?
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'The first rocks to be formed due to this solidification were Precambrian or crystalline rocks… These are igneous rocks, and form the starting point in the rock cycle. All subsequent rocks such as metamorphic and sedimentary rocks are derived from these rocks.'
Answer: C.
tips: Rock cycle starts with igneous rock (cooling of molten material).

similar_questions.stem: Precambrian rocks cover about what share of Eritrea?
explanation_steps: Textbook: about 60%. Answer: C.

questions.review_flag: The Eritrean Precambrian basement is largely metamorphic (schist, gneiss); the key follows the textbook's statement that igneous rocks came first.

questions.stem: The process by which water changes from liquid to solid state is
explanation_steps: Liquid → solid = freezing (at 0 °C for pure water).
Condensation is gas → liquid, evaporation liquid → gas, sublimation solid → gas directly. Answer: E.
tips: Name each change of state by its start and end.

similar_questions.stem: Water vapour turning into droplets to form clouds is
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

questions.stem: The total life span of the earth is estimated to be
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'the earth is 4.6 billion years old.'
The question's 'total life span' means the age of the earth so far. Answer: E.
tips: Earth ≈ 4.6 billion years; Precambrian ends ≈ 600 million years ago (textbook).

similar_questions.stem: The oldest geological era is the
explanation_steps: Answer: D.

questions.review_flag: Wording: ‘total life span’ is used for the earth's age to date (4.6 billion years).

questions.stem: All regions share common characteristics including
explanation_steps: Every region has a location, an area (extent) and boundaries, and regions are arranged in a hierarchy (smaller regions inside larger ones).
Answer: E.
tips: Region characteristics: location, extent (size), boundary, homogeneity, hierarchy.

similar_questions.stem: A region defined by one or more common physical or human features is a
explanation_steps: Answer: A.

questions.stem: The Eritrean river that has the <u>highest</u> volume of water discharge is
explanation_steps: Textbook Table 2.1: annual discharge – Setit 8–10 billion m³, Barka 400–800 million m³, Gash 200–400 million m³. Setit is Eritrea's only perennial river.
Answer: A.
tips: Setit (Tekeze) = perennial, largest discharge; Mereb = longest (560 km, textbook).

similar_questions.stem: Eritrea's only perennial river is the
explanation_steps: Answer: C.

questions.stem: The type of erosion where thin layer of soil is removed by overland flow is called
explanation_steps: Sheet erosion removes a thin, even layer of topsoil over a wide area by overland flow (sheet wash).
Rills are small channels, gullies deep ones; splash is raindrop impact. Answer: C.
tips: Order of severity: splash → sheet → rill → gully.

similar_questions.stem: Deep channels cut by concentrated run-off that cannot be removed by ploughing are
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

questions.stem: Ground water in Eritrea can be easily depleted by
explanation_steps: The textbook (problems of water resources in the Highlands): '(a) Groundwater is easily depleted due to heavy pumping for irrigation. (b) Siltation is a serious problem in the surface water development.'
Siltation fills dams and ponds (surface water); it does not deplete groundwater. Answer: A.
tips: Groundwater problem = over-pumping; surface water problem = siltation.

similar_questions.stem: Siltation is mainly a problem for
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

questions.stem: The ability of air to hold moisture largely depends on
explanation_steps: Warm air can hold much more water vapour than cold air; cooling air to its dew point makes it saturated and causes condensation.
Answer: B.
tips: Warm air = sponge; cool it and it 'squeezes out' water.

similar_questions.stem: Relative humidity usually rises at night because

options.B: the air cools and can hold less vapour

explanation_steps: Answer: B.

questions.stem: The local name for spring rainfall in Eritrea is
explanation_steps: The small spring rains (March–April, from moist air from the Gulf of Aden/Indian Ocean – textbook) are locally called Azmera.
Kremti = main summer rainy season (textbook); Bahri = the eastern escarpment/coastal zone with winter rain; Hagay = the dry season; Qewei = the hot season. Answer: C.
tips: Kremti (summer), Azmera (spring), Bahri (winter rains on the escarpment/coast).

similar_questions.stem: The main summer rainy season in Eritrea is locally called
explanation_steps: Textbook: 'This rainy summer season is locally known as Kremti.' Answer: B.

textbook_ref.note: The textbook describes the spring rain but gives only 'Kremti' as a local name.

questions.review_flag: Textbook gap: ‘Azmera’ is not named in the textbook (only ‘Kremti’); keyed from local usage.

questions.stem: Changes in weather and climate are due to
explanation_steps: Latitude (sun's angle), altitude (lapse rate), ocean currents (warm/cold coasts) and distance from the sea (continentality) all control temperature and rainfall.
Answer: E.
tips: Climate controls: latitude, altitude, distance from sea, ocean currents, relief, winds.

similar_questions.stem: Asmara is cooler than Massawa mainly because of
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which of the following cities has the highest potential evapo-transpiration?
explanation_steps: Textbook Table 3.3 (annual PET, mm): Tessenei 2064, Akordat 2051, Assab 1974, Massawa 1944, Asmara 1507, Adi Keih 532.7.
Of the options Tessenei has the highest PET (Assab is a close second). Answer: E.
tips: PET is high in the hot lowlands (both the Red Sea coast and the western lowlands) and falls with altitude.

similar_questions.stem: Evapo-transpiration and altitude show

options.D: a relationship only on the coast

explanation_steps: Textbook: PET decreases as altitude increases. Answer: B.

questions.review_flag: Many students will pick Assab (hottest coast); the textbook table gives Tessenei (2064 mm) slightly above Assab (1974 mm).

questions.stem: What is the difference between weather and climate? (2 points)
questions.answer: Weather is the condition of the atmosphere (temperature, rainfall, humidity, wind, pressure, cloud) at a particular place over a short period – hours or days. Climate is the average weather condition of a place or region measured over a long period, usually 30–35 years.
explanation_steps: Textbook: weather = short-term, day-to-day state of the atmosphere; climate = long-term average (about 30+ years) of weather elements over a large area.
marking_points: 1 point: weather = atmospheric condition of a place for a short time (day-to-day)
1 point: climate = average weather over a long period (≈30 years) / large area
tips: Key contrast: time span (short vs long) and scale (particular day vs average).

similar_questions.stem: Classify: 'Asmara has cool, dry winters and a rainy summer'. Is this weather or climate?
similar_questions.answer: Climate – it describes the average seasonal pattern over many years.
explanation_steps: A statement about a long-term pattern is climate; 'it is raining in Asmara today' is weather.

questions.stem: Write a short note on the following components of soil. (2 points) 3.1 Organic matter 3.2 Inorganic matter
questions.answer:
3.1 Organic matter: the decayed (and decaying) remains of plants and animals, plus living soil organisms; decomposed it forms humus, which gives the soil a dark colour, supplies plant nutrients (N, P, S) and improves water-holding capacity and structure.
3.2 Inorganic matter: the mineral part of the soil – particles of sand, silt and clay formed by the weathering of the parent rock; it forms the bulk of the soil and supplies mineral nutrients (K, Ca, Mg…). (Air and water fill the pore spaces between the particles.)
explanation_steps: Textbook: soil consists of mineral (inorganic) matter from weathered rock, organic matter (humus) from decomposed plants and animals, water and air.
marking_points: 1 point: organic matter = decomposed plant/animal remains (humus) – adds nutrients / holds water
1 point: inorganic matter = mineral particles (sand, silt, clay) from weathered parent rock
tips: Organic = once living; inorganic = from rocks.

similar_questions.stem: Why do dark soils usually indicate high fertility?
similar_questions.answer: The dark colour comes from a large amount of humus (organic matter), which supplies nutrients and holds water.
explanation_steps: Textbook: black or dark brown colours indicate much humus and high fertility.

questions.stem: Mention two types of mountains. (2 points)
questions.answer: Any two of: fold mountains (e.g. Himalayas, Alps, Atlas); block mountains (e.g. Mount Gedem in Eritrea); volcanic mountains (e.g. Kilimanjaro); residual mountains (worn down by erosion).
explanation_steps: Textbook (5.2 Mountains): i) Fold mountains – formed when layers of sediment are compressed and folded; ii) Block mountains – land between two faults is raised (Mount Gedem); iii) Volcanic mountains – molten material comes to the surface and solidifies; iv) Residual mountains – height reduced by erosion.
marking_points: 1 point each for any two: fold, block, volcanic, residual mountains
tips: Classify by origin: folding, faulting, volcanism, erosion.

similar_questions.stem: How is a block mountain formed?
similar_questions.answer: When the land between two parallel faults is pushed up (or the land on either side sinks), leaving a raised block (horst) with steep sides.
explanation_steps: Textbook: Mount Gedem near Massawa is an example.

questions.stem: What are the two sub-divisions of the Dry Climate? (1 point)
questions.answer: Desert (arid) and steppe (semi-arid) climates. The textbook discusses the two most important as the Sub-tropical Desert Climate and the Sub-tropical Steppe Climate (its four types are sub-tropical desert, sub-tropical steppe, mid-latitude desert and mid-latitude steppe).
explanation_steps: Textbook 1.2.2: 'The dry climates can be classified into four types… sub-tropical desert, sub-tropical steppe, mid-latitude desert and mid-latitude steppe. The two most important sub-divisions are… i) Sub-tropical Desert Climate… ii) Subtropical Steppe Climate.'
marking_points: ½ point: (sub-tropical) desert climate
½ point: (sub-tropical) steppe / semi-arid climate (mid-latitude desert/steppe also accepted)
tips: Desert = < about 250 mm rain; steppe = semi-arid grassland on the desert margins.

similar_questions.stem: Where are sub-tropical deserts mostly located?
similar_questions.answer: In the western and central parts of continents in the sub-tropical latitudes (about 15°–30° N and S), e.g. the Sahara, Kalahari, Arabian and Australian deserts.
explanation_steps: Textbook: largest portions in sub-tropical latitudes of the western and central portions of continents.

questions.stem: List two types of load of a river with an example for each type. (2 points)
questions.answer: Any two of: (1) Solution (dissolved load) – dissolved minerals such as calcium carbonate or salts; (2) Suspension (suspended load) – fine particles such as clay and silt (and fine sand); (3) Saltation – sand and small pebbles bounced along the bed; (4) Traction (bed load) – large stones and boulders rolled along the bed.
explanation_steps: Textbook: 'The dissolved materials are carried in solution. The fine particles such as silt, clay and sand are carried in suspension. Large materials are rolled and bounced along the bed.'
marking_points: 1 point per type with a correct example (max 2): solution – dissolved salts; suspension – silt/clay; saltation – sand/pebbles; traction – boulders
tips: Name the type AND give a matching example for full marks.

similar_questions.stem: Why does a river in flood carry larger boulders than in the dry season?
similar_questions.answer: A flood has more water and higher speed, so more energy to move heavy material by traction.
explanation_steps: Textbook: carrying ability depends on the amount of water and the speed of the river.

questions.stem: Write a short description on how a dissected plateau is formed. (2 points)
questions.answer: A dissected plateau forms when rivers flowing across a plateau (a high, flat-topped upland) erode it by vertical down-cutting, cutting deep, steep-sided valleys and gorges. Over time the once-continuous flat surface is broken up into separate flat-topped remnants (mesas, buttes) separated by valleys – e.g. parts of the Eritrean highland plateau cut by the Anseba, Mereb and escarpment rivers.
explanation_steps: Textbook (5.4 Plateaus): 'iv) Dissected Plateaus – This type of plateau is formed when rivers erode and cut the plateau into deep valleys.'
marking_points: 1 point: rivers erode/cut down into a plateau (vertical erosion)
1 point: forming deep valleys that break the plateau into separate uplands/flat-topped remnants
tips: Two ideas: (1) a plateau exists; (2) rivers erode it into deep valleys leaving uplands between them.

similar_questions.stem: How is a volcanic (lava) plateau formed?
similar_questions.answer: Large amounts of lava pour out quietly through fissures, spread over wide areas and solidify in layers, building a high flat plateau (e.g. the basalt plateau around Asmara).
explanation_steps: Textbook: volcanic plateaus form when large amounts of molten material come out and spread over the surface.

questions.stem: Write a short explanation on any two processes of weathering. (3 points)
questions.answer:
Any two of:
(1) Physical (mechanical) weathering – rocks break into smaller pieces without chemical change: e.g. in deserts, high day temperatures make the outer layers expand and cold nights make them contract, so they crack and peel off (exfoliation); water freezing in cracks expands and splits rocks (frost action).
(2) Chemical weathering – minerals in the rock are changed or dissolved by water, oxygen and acids: e.g. oxidation (iron minerals rust, turning rocks red), carbonation/solution (rain water with CO₂ dissolves limestone), hydration and hydrolysis (feldspar → clay).
(3) Biological weathering – living things break rocks: plant roots grow into cracks and widen them; burrowing animals and lichens also break and dissolve rock.
explanation_steps: Textbook (2.1 Soil formation): 'There are two types of weathering. Physical weathering: During the day-time, there is high temperature… (expansion and contraction). Chemical weathering: This type of weathering involves the (chemical change of rock minerals)…' Biological weathering by roots and organisms is also accepted.
marking_points: 1½ points per process (max 3): correct name (½) + explanation of how it breaks down rock with an example (1)
tips: For each process: name it (½–1 point) and explain how it breaks rock (1 point).

similar_questions.stem: Why is chemical weathering faster in hot, wet regions than in deserts?
similar_questions.answer: Chemical reactions need water and go faster at high temperatures, so hot humid climates (tropical rainforest) weather rocks chemically fastest; deserts lack water, so physical weathering dominates.
explanation_steps: Relate each process to climate.

questions.stem: Mention two requirements for development. (2 points)
questions.answer: Any two of: access to resources (natural resources and human resources/skills); capital (investment from saving); technology; an educated, skilled and healthy population (human capital); peace and stability; good governance/effective institutions; infrastructure.
explanation_steps: Textbook (4.1.2 Requirements for development): access to resources is a fundamental requirement; capital is another prerequisite; technology and skilled people; peace and stability are critical.
marking_points: 1 point each for any two correct requirements (resources, capital, technology, skilled/educated labour, peace and stability, good governance, infrastructure)
tips: Resources, capital, technology, skilled people, peace – 'R-C-T-S-P'.

similar_questions.stem: Why is peace and stability a requirement for development?
similar_questions.answer: War destroys infrastructure and capital, diverts resources to defence, stops investment and trade and displaces people, so production cannot grow.
explanation_steps: Textbook: peace and stability are critical for investment and building infrastructure.

questions.stem: List two features formed in the upper course of a river. (2 points)
questions.answer: Any two of: V-shaped valleys; gorges (canyons); interlocking spurs; waterfalls; rapids; potholes.
explanation_steps: Textbook (2.2 Upper course – youth or torrent stage): vertical erosion dominates, forming a) V-shaped valleys, b) gorges (canyons), c) interlocking spurs, and also waterfalls and rapids where hard rock bands cross the river.
marking_points: 1 point each for any two: V-shaped valley, gorge/canyon, interlocking spurs, waterfall, rapids, potholes
tips: Upper course = steep, fast, vertical erosion; middle = meanders; lower = flood plains, levees, deltas.

similar_questions.stem: List two features formed in the lower course of a river.
similar_questions.answer: Any two: flood plain, levees, deltas, ox-bow lakes, distributaries.
explanation_steps: Deposition dominates in the old (plain) stage.
